newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cambodia's Ranariddh says he sole legitimate power.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Ranariddh says he sole legitimate power.

text.p: First Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh said on Saturday he had become head of Cambodia's only legitimate government as a result of an alleged coup attempt by his rival, Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.

"At this time, the sole legitimate government of Cambodia is the one over which I preside, given legitimacy by the free and democratic elections organised by the United Nations in 1993 and by the confidence of the Cambodian people," he said.

Hun Sen "has attempted a coup d'etat in having his troops intervene on orders of his party, the CPP (Cambodian People's Party), in Phnom Penh...causing the death of numerous innocent civilians," he said in a statement faxed to news agencies in Paris, where Ranariddh was said to be visiting family.

The statement was the second in hours issued in the first prime minister's name in Paris after an outbreak of fighting in the Cambodian capital between groups of soldiers loyal to Hun Sen and others answering to Ranariddh.
The clashes started after Hun Sen ordered a crackdown on "illegal troops" under Ranariddh's command.
In an earlier statement, the first prime minister accused Hun Sen of seeking to stage a coup against him in order to derail democratic elections set for May 1998.
In the second statement, Ranariddh said the fighting had revealed Hun Sen's "supreme ambition: To win power which he feared losing in the next elections in May 1998."

He said he wanted to alert the international community to "the serious consequences of Mr Hun Sen's criminal actions" and urged all Cambodian forces "to resist the attempted coup and violence mounted by Mr Hun Sen and his criminal band".
